stops.name: Winchester, the beheading of Meleagant
stops.campa: Godefroi de Leigni, who finishes what Chrétien left unwritten, brings Meleagant to Arthur's own court a year later to press his accusation again and force the duel neither king could put off forever. Lancelot cuts through him without the mercy he shows other men: the right arm falls at one clean stroke, the nose-guard is smashed back through three teeth, the helmet is unlaced and the head comes off. Not a soul present feels any pity. The court that watched a stranger ride off behind a dwarf's cart watches him walk back in as the best knight living.

stops.name: Corbenic (unlocated), the deception of Brisen
stops.campa: Corbenic, castle of the wounded Fisher King Pelles and keeper of the Sangreal itself, has no fixed place on any map the romances agree on; this record marks it, honestly, in the borderlands its illustrators and modern gazetteers most often guess at, not a claimed real site. Pelles' daughter Elaine loves Lancelot past reason and cannot have him, since his whole heart is sworn elsewhere; her handmaid Brisen, skilled in enchantment, brews a wine that makes him believe he lies with Guinevere in a chamber lit only by candles. He does not learn the truth until morning, and by morning Galahad is already begun.

stops.name: Winchester, Guinevere's discovery and the banishment
stops.campa: Word of the deception reaches Camelot, as such things always do, and Guinevere's fury when she learns of it is not jealousy of a rival but the particular rage of a woman who trusted a story could stay simple. She banishes Lancelot from her sight and from court in one sentence, without appeal, and gives no man leave to soften it. He has weathered swords, enchantments, and a year's captivity for her sake, but this single sentence undoes him more completely than any of it; he leaves the hall already half out of his own mind.

stops.name: The wild country (unlocated), two years mad
stops.campa: Grief and shame close over him at once: he leaps from an open window rather than be looked at, and something in him breaks that no surgeon can set. For two years he wanders the wild country naked or half-clothed, sleeping rough, fighting shepherds for scraps, known to no one and answering to no name at all, not even a false one; that will come later. The court that praised him as the best living knight has no idea where he is; the man who crossed a bridge of swords for the queen now cannot be trusted with a blade at all.

stops.name: Corbenic, the cure and the Joyous Isle
stops.campa: Elaine finds him at last, raving in a garden at Corbenic, and has him carried within reach of the vessel that healed her own father's wound. Brought before the Sangreal itself, still wrapped in its samite, he is cured on the spot, his wits restored as suddenly as they left him. Ashamed to return to Camelot as the man who broke, he takes Elaine's offer instead: a hidden island he names the Joyous Isle, and a false name to wear on it, Le Chevaler Mal Fet, the knight that hath trespassed. Some years of half-borrowed quiet follow, until Ector and Percivale find him.

stops.name: Winchester, the Pentecost vigil and Galahad's arrival
stops.campa: Years pass at court in a peace this record folds rather than pads with invented incident, until a Pentecost eve when a strange old man leads a young knight into the hall and sets him in the one seat at the Round Table always left empty, the Siege Perilous, which has burned every man before who dared it. The boy takes the seat and lives; new letters of gold appear on its edge naming him. Lancelot, watching, already half-guesses what no one has yet said aloud: the boy's face is his own at that age, and the mother's name is Elaine of Corbenic.

stops.name: A hermitage in the forest (unlocated), the sin named
stops.campa: On the road of the quest a hermit stops Lancelot and reads his whole life back to him without flattery: the greatest knight living, and the least fit of all the fellowship to see the thing he is riding to find. Pride in his own prowess, the hermit says, and the love of a married queen carried for years without repentance, have made him a knight of the world's honor and not of God's. Lancelot does not argue the charge. He confesses fourteen years of hidden sin, weeps, and rides on anyway, because the quest is the one road left that he refuses to turn back from.
stops.quote: never did I battle all only for God's sake, but for to win worship and to cause me to be the better beloved and little or nought I thanked God of it
stops.quote_source: Malory, Le Morte d'Arthur, Book XIII, Chapter XX (Lancelot's confession to the hermit)

stops.name: Corbenic, struck down before the Grail
stops.campa: The quest brings him back, of all castles in Britain, to Corbenic, where his own son was conceived by a trick he never consented to. A voice warns him at the chamber door not to enter, for what is within is not for sinful eyes; inside he sees, through incense and candlelight, a table of silver and the Sangreal itself, and a mass no living hand should come near without leave. He goes in anyway, to help what he takes for a failing priest, and a breath mixed with fire strikes him down. He lies as a dead man four and twenty days and as many nights.

stops.name: Winchester, Agravain's plot and the ambush
stops.campa: Years of guarded peace follow the quest's end, years this record does not pad with invented incident, until Agravain and Mordred, who have hated the secret longer than they have hidden it, tell Arthur outright what the whole court has half-known and never said. Arthur, cornered by his own nephews into acting, rides out hunting and leaves the queen's door watched. Lancelot, warned too late by nothing but habit, comes to her chamber that night anyway and finds a dozen armed knights waiting instead of the queen alone; he kills his way out through men he has fought beside for years.

stops.name: Carlisle, the queen condemned
stops.campa: Arthur, bound by his own law more than by his own wish, condemns Guinevere to be burned outside Carlisle for treason, though the record notes plainly that he does it with a broken heart and no joy in it. His nephews Gareth and Gaheris are made to attend under protest and refuse, out of love for both the queen and Lancelot, to wear armor to the burning, an unarmed mercy that will cost them everything within the hour. The queen is led out in a plain smock to the stake in the field, and the fire is already being laid when the first shout goes up from the watching hill.

stops.name: Carlisle, the rescue and the accidental deaths
stops.campa: Lancelot's spies signal from the hill and he comes down on the crowd at full gallop with his kinsmen, cutting the queen loose from the stake in a press of steel and smoke. In the crush he kills men he never meant to touch: Gareth and Gaheris, unarmed as they swore to be, go down under blows meant for armored strangers, and Lancelot does not even know whose bodies he has made until the field clears. It is the single stroke from which the fellowship of the Round Table never recovers, since Gawain will forgive the queen, forgive the war, but never forgive his brothers' deaths.

stops.name: Bamburgh (Joyous Gard), the fifteen-week siege
stops.campa: Lancelot carries the queen north to his own castle, and it earns its name again in the hardest way: Joyous Gard becomes the one refuge left to a rescued queen and a knight now called traitor by half the men who once called him friend. Arthur, driven by Gawain's grief past every wish of his own heart, brings the strength of the realm to besiege it. Fifteen weeks the siege holds, Lancelot provisioned and unwilling the whole time to strike a real blow at his own king, sending out only enough force to hold the walls and no more.
